items.title: Canada is helping create a healthier, stronger world for everyone
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>Malnutrition doesn’t happen overnight... and it is not a choice.

When nutritious food becomes hard to get, women and children are often the most affected.

That’s why Canada is investing in something bigger: prevention.  

Global hunger and nutrition are not distant issues, they are shared challenges with shared impacts.

Canada’s nutrition support in emergencies and investments in long term nutrition don’t just help communities abroad, they help build a more stable, secure, and prosperous world that also benefits people in Canada.</article>

items.title: Every kid deserves an education
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>How strongly would you fight for your child’s education? What if your family was facing a crisis?

Unfortunately, during a crisis, education often takes a backseat.

Being forced out of your home is bad enough, losing access to school makes it worse. Yet children in refugee camps face many challenges that make them more likely to drop out of school.

Conflict can put children's futures at risk, with impacts felt in Canada and around the world.

Canada continues to support kids affected by crisis.

Because kids everywhere deserve an education.
#TogetherForHumanity  #HumanitarianCrisis  #WithRefugees  #SolidarityInAction</article>

items.title: Team Canada Trade Mission heading to India
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>Canada has what the world needs, and we are open for business! 

In May, Canada was pleased to welcome India’s Minister of Commerce and Industry, Piyush Goyal, and the largest trade delegation India has ever sent to Canada—or anywhere in the world!  

To further advance the Canada-India relationship, Minister Sidhu will lead the #TeamCanadaTradeMission to Mumbai and Bengaluru, India, in October. The trade mission will help to unlock new commercial partnerships in a market of more than 1.4 billion people—the world’s fastest-growing major economy! 

If you are a business and want to join the trade mission, apply now:   

https://www.tradecommissioner.gc.ca/en/trade-events-training/2026/10/team-canada-trade-mission-india.html</article>

items.title: Listening to local voices: Canada and UNDP in Bangladesh
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>What does meaningful development look like on the ground?

During a visit to Rajshahi, Canada’s High Commissioner to Bangladesh, Ajit Singh, met with indigenous communities to hear about their experiences, priorities and aspirations.

Through its partnership with UNDP, Canada supports inclusive, locally driven development that puts communities at the heart of solutions.

@UNDP | @UNDPBangladesh</article>

items.title: Why it matters: Global health security
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>In just days, a disease anywhere can become a health security crisis everywhere.  

Canada works with experienced partners worldwide,  investing in essential health services, such as access to primary care, outbreak preparedness, surveillance and rapid screening, as well as strengthening the capacity to prevent, detect and respond to biological threats. 

These efforts save lives, build resilient communities and reduce crises. 

This includes Canada’s active support to contain the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda and to strengthen preparedness in neighbouring countries like South Sudan. 

Because making a difference in the world  makes a difference for Canadians, too.</article>

items.title: RUTFs have been saving lives for 30 years
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>This year, we’re marking 30 years of a life-saving breakthrough.

Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Food (RUTF) has helped millions of severely malnourished children recover and thrive. 

Why does it work? It’s simple, safe, affordable, and easy to use. 

Canada is proud to support UNICEF to deliver RUTF to those who need it most. 

This small sachet still has a big impact 🌍✨ 

#Nutrition #GlobalHealth #SaveLives</article>

items.title: Canada's 2024-2025 International Assistance Report
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>Partnership is our greatest multiplier. 🤝🌍 

In a shifting global landscape, Canada is focusing on results.  
Our 2024 to 2025 International Assistance Report shows how 20 federal departments are working together to tackle challenges head-on. 

Why this matters at home:  
✅ Economic security: Helping partners build resilient economies 
✅ Stability: Creating a more predictable world for trade 
✅ Resilience: Smart investments today that prevent the crises of tomorrow 

When we build a safer world, we build a stronger Canada. 

🔗 For more info, click the link ➡️ https://international.canada.ca/en/global-affairs/corporate/reports/international-assistance-report/report-overview-2025</article>

items.title: Episode 2 – Why it matters: Global health
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>We live in a highly connected world. In just days, a disease can spread across borders, turning a local issue into a global challenge. But Canada is taking action. 

By working with experienced partners, Canada is investing in: 

🍎 essential nutrition and clean water 
💉 life-saving immunizations 
🏥 stronger health care systems 
🩺 health worker training 
🤍maternal care support  

Why does this matter for Canadians?

True to its values, Canada strives for a better future for all.  
By caring for the most vulnerable and building resilient communities worldwide, we ensure:  

✅ safer travel for Canadians abroad 
✅ less pressure on international resources 
✅ a stronger, more stable economy here at home   

Making a difference in the world makes a difference for Canadians, too. 

Learn more about our work: https://www.international.gc.ca/world-monde/issues_development-enjeux_developpement/global_health-sante_mondiale/index.aspx?lang=eng   

#GlobalHealth #Canada #PublicHealth #Innovation #CdnPoli</article>

items.title: How Division Can Be Manufactured
items.author: Global Affairs Canada
items.content:
<article>That heated debate in your feed? It might be manufactured outrage. Some foreign regimes exploit real tensions, target communities, amplify extremes and weaponize anger to divide us. 
 
Learn their tactics and #ThinkBeforeYouShare 
 
See how Canada is taking action: https://www.international.gc.ca/world-monde/issues_development-enjeux_developpement/peace_security-paix_securite/combatt-disinformation-desinformation.aspx?lang=eng</article>
